title: Evidence
description: Federal Rules of Evidence, Classes 1–19 (Fisher, Evidence, 4th ed.): jury secrecy, relevance and 403, the policy exclusions, character evidence and 404(b), impeachment and the rape shield, hearsay and its exceptions, the Confrontation Clause, Bruton, the right to present a defense, and lay and expert opinion. Includes the outline, rule chart, flowcharts, flashcards, and bar-style practice questions.

Evidence_Condensed_Outline.docx.title: Evidence Outline
Evidence_Condensed_Outline.docx.description: Condensed exam outline of Classes 1–19 on the Fall 2026 syllabus (Fisher pp. 1–783). Part I covers the Federal Rules, jury secrecy under 606(b), relevance, conditional relevance, and 403. Part II covers the specialized relevance rules, 407–411. Part III covers character evidence: the propensity ban, 404(b), Huddleston, 413–415, the defendant's and victim's character, and habit. Part IV covers impeachment under 607–609 and the rape shield. Part V covers competency, the definition of hearsay, opposing parties' statements, prior statements of witnesses, and the 803, 804, and 807 exceptions. Part VI covers the Confrontation Clause from Crawford through Smith v. Arizona. Part VII covers completeness, Bruton, and Chambers. Part VIII covers lay and expert opinion from the Week 10 reading. Rule and tip boxes throughout, and a card for every principal case with its class.

Evidence_Master_Outline.docx.description: Full master outline of Classes 1–19, swept against all 19 slide decks and the Week 1–10 readings, with every problem, the slides' answers, and an errata log. Kept off the public site. Use it as the reference when making questions, flowcharts, and flashcards for this subject.

2Evidence_Rule_Chart (with class slides).title: Evidence Rule Chart/outline
2Evidence_Rule_Chart (with class slides).description: The master rule chart for Weeks 1–5. Each rule is explained in plain English with a note on what to watch out for. Rows tagged by class come from the Class 1–10 lecture slides, and there are notes on what the midterm covers.

Evidence_Rule_Flowcharts.html.title: Evidence Flowcharts
Evidence_Rule_Flowcharts.html.description: Interactive decision charts for Weeks 1–5. Zoom and pan around each chart, walk through a rule one step at a time, and search all nine charts. Covers relevance (401–403), the policy rules (407–411), character evidence, 404(b), impeachment, 609 convictions, the 412 rape shield, and 606(b) jury secrecy.

FRE_Rule_Cards.html.title: FRE Rule Cards
FRE_Rule_Cards.html.description: Flashcards for the Federal Rules of Evidence in Weeks 1–5. Pick your topics, flip each card, and rate yourself with a tap or a swipe. Missed cards come back sooner, and your mastery is saved in your browser.

Evidence_MCQ_Conceptual.html.title: Evidence Rules easy Drill
Evidence_MCQ_Conceptual.html.description: Conceptual multiple-choice questions for Weeks 1–5, weighted toward the Federal Rules. The answer order reshuffles every time you load the page, so you can't memorize the letters.

Evidence_MCQ_Application (strict).html.title: Evidence BAR style questions 1
Evidence_MCQ_Application (strict).html.description: Bar-level application questions for Weeks 1–5. Each question sets two or three rules against each other and turns on a single fact. Every answer choice has its own explanation, and the set includes one-fact variations and a coverage map.

Evidence_MCQ_Application (Classes 1-10)..title: Evidence BAR style questions 2
Evidence_MCQ_Application (Classes 1-10)..description: A second, all-new set of bar-style application questions covering Classes 1–10. Every answer choice has its own explanation. Includes one-fact variations and a coverage map of all 157 outline items.

Evidence_Mock_Midterm.html.title: Evidence Mock Midterm
Evidence_Mock_Midterm.html.description: A timed practice exam for the night before the midterm: 60 new bar-style questions on Classes 1–10, in four 15-question parts that each cover every topic at the real exam’s 30-minute pace. Answers stay hidden until you submit. Then you get your score by topic, the rules to review, and an explanation for every choice.

Evidence_Mock_Midterm_II.html.title: Evidence Mock Midterm II
Evidence_Mock_Midterm_II.html.description: A second timed practice exam: 60 more new bar-style questions on Classes 1–10, with no fact patterns repeated from the first. It has the same four 15-question parts, each covering every topic at the real exam’s 30-minute pace, and draws on textbook problems the first exam didn’t use. Answers stay hidden until you submit. Then you get your score by topic, the rules to review, and an explanation for every choice.
